limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The executed credit agreement and the 2029 notes indenture were not supplied, so covenant definitions, scheduled amortization and baskets cannot be established for any period and no covenant headroom is stated. Severity High. Supply both documents before covenant or amortization statements are made. - Pro forma EBITDA for the Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators acquisitions is not stated, so leverage and cover on a full-period basis are not calculable at 2026-01-31, 2026-05-02 and 2026-08-01. Severity Medium. Use issuer-stated pro forma figures when they are published. - Scheduled principal amortization of the term loans is not itemized, so the maturity table is by final maturity and the current portion of debt of USD 28,397 thousand at 2026-08-01 cannot be broken down. Severity Medium. Obtain the amortization schedule from the credit agreement. - Cash interest paid for the last-twelve-months periods is built from year-to-date disclosures and only partly reflects the larger borrowings, so cover on cash interest is flattered. Severity Medium. Read it with the ratio on interest expense, net in the calculation register. - The Adjusted EBITDA add-back set differs between fiscal 2026 and the first half of fiscal 2027, so last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA mixes two definitions. Severity Medium. Quote it only beside reported EBITDA and label the definition. - The printed fiscal 2026 add-backs sum to 737.9 against a printed adjusted figure of 737.7, so the EBITDA bridge is not stated and every bridge amount is not supplied. Severity Low. The issuer states that totals may not add due to rounding. - The statements print a dash for some lines with no activity, for example income taxes payable at 2026-05-02 and 2026-08-01 and credit agreement borrowings in the fiscal 2027 periods; each is shown as not supplied and never read as zero. Severity Low. Confirm nil activity from the notes if a figure is needed. - Some lines are printed in only some filings, for example loss on debt extinguishment in the annual statements and the bridge loan lines for fiscal 2026 only; they are shown as not supplied for the filings that omit them. Severity Low. No action needed unless a line total is rebuilt. - No balance sheet at 2024-01-27 is in the sources, so fiscal 2024 net debt and leverage are not calculable, and the fiscal 2024 income and cash flow columns are not tabulated. Severity Low. Add the fiscal 2025 annual report if a longer history is wanted. - Finance lease obligations of USD 2,700 thousand at 2026-08-01 are carried inside debt but their ranking, security, rate and principal are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and the maturity table. Severity Low. Obtain the lease terms if they become material. - The revolver pricing is not stated separately from term loan A in the filings. Severity Low. Obtain the pricing grid from the credit agreement. - Communications Adjusted EBITDA for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 is 192.4 in the results presentation and 192.5 in the filed quarterly report; the filed figure is used. Severity Low. No action. - The fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 is not tabulated as a discrete quarter because only the annual and nine-month statements and a presentation reconciliation carry it. Severity Low. Derive it by difference only if a quarterly series is needed. - Some dashboard cells are not printed in the sources read, such as year-on-year revenue growth for fiscal 2025 and the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and organic growth for periods the presentations do not report, and the segment schedule shows no corporate revenue because none is printed. Severity Low. No action unless those series are needed. - The customer-sponsored receivable sale programs state their discount fee but not the amounts of receivables sold, so their size as a funding source is not established. Severity Medium. Obtain the volumes from the issuer.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The main strength is liquidity with a long runway: USD 1,086.5 million of liquidity, of which USD 746.4 million is undrawn revolver, and no maturity before the USD 500.0 million of 2029 notes mean a spending shock can be absorbed without a refinancing. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Dycom presents an adequate business profile supported by backlog, liquidity of USD 1,086.5 million and a Building Systems growth segment, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rose with two debt-funded acquisitions, customer concentration and a weakening Communications margin. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but seasonal, with first-half free cash flow of USD -54.2 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth lowering leverage before the 2029 notes and on financial policy staying within covenants. spans.text: # CP-1 handoff: Financial foundation for DYCOM INDUSTRIES INC
## Request

Financial foundation for DYCOM INDUSTRIES INC (issuer id dy), as of 2026-11-05, for the credit snapshot pathway. It sets the reported statements, debt, liquidity and ratios for fiscal 2025, fiscal 2026 and the first half of fiscal 2027 on one USD basis. It draws no independent credit recommendation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 (fiscal 2026, 53 weeks) | 2026-03-09 (signature date) | d3cce30e8b33b40ee726fca361a4ac5af2d47cfff9b57a3f36d911b5b73b8e31 | Audited statements, debt note, Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest, segment data, covenants |

| 10-Q_2025-10-25_dy-20251025.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2025 (third quarter of fiscal 2026) | 2025-11-20 (signature date) | 629b328324cc0ef5393e62b61d8db6e3a1e48e205e2a0f26575592aea3390dd7 | Debt terms in force before the December 2025 refinancing, noted as superseded |

| 10-Q_2026-05-02_dy-20260502.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 2, 2026 (first quarter of fiscal 2027) | 2026-05-28 (signature date) | 237d7d80121afc72a5bb1b73d79141b69d6396b9608af9b8f3dec2db64be0f4f | Interim statements and balance sheet at 2026-05-02, constructed periods, segment results, covenant terms |

| EX-99.2_2026-03-04_q42026presentationmateri.htm.jsonl | Fourth quarter fiscal 2026 results presentation (exhibit to a current report) | 2026-03-04 | 6988c6bbc189fb06cb090ad132fb7c67f67f6d428cb3b75cae839c0b2d040376 | Backlog and free cash flow comparatives, organic growth |

| EX-99.2_2026-05-27_q12027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl | First quarter fiscal 2027 results presentation (exhibit to a current report) | 2026-05-27 | fb3e1da73422f05d34562fe3208f0c4af7eb6fffd05db64f60aea98effba2a9e | Cross-check of segment Adjusted EBITDA |

Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 a9666727b0d5884c6687d8beafbe462222a8e3c05442392537cb06c514f19ec1.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage has eased since the acquisition financing, with net debt at 2.73x reported EBITDA at 2026-08-01 against 2.99x at the year end, but earnings include the acquired businesses only part-period, so the improvement is incomplete.

Cash interest cover of 10.49x flatters the position because cash interest paid over the last twelve months only partly reflects the larger borrowings; reported EBITDA covered interest expense by 7.64x in the first half of fiscal 2027. The revolver was undrawn with USD 746.4 million of availability and cash was USD 340.08 million, while the credit agreement was not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.
Basis: calculation C29; calculation C27; calculation C33; calculation C34; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 21; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Gross debt to reported EBITDA fell from 4.00x at the fiscal 2026 year end to 3.11x at 2026-08-01 while carrying-value debt was almost unchanged, so the whole improvement is earnings growth rather than repayment. Net debt rose over the same period because cash fell, yet net leverage still fell from 2.99x to 2.73x, which means EBITDA grew faster than net debt. Last-twelve-months EBITDA includes Power Solutions only from 2025-12-23 and National Technology Integrators only from 2026-07-02, so leverage on a full-period basis would be lower, but the sources state no pro forma EBITDA and none is worked out here.
Basis: calculation C27; calculation C29; calculation C15; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 27

Issuer-adjusted EBITDA is higher than reported EBITDA in each of the four ratio periods and gives 2.94x gross and 2.58x net leverage at 2026-08-01, but its add-back set changed between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, so the adjusted figures are a mixed definition and the ratios here use reported EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C21

Operating cash flow converts weakly in the first half of each year: it was 0.14x reported EBITDA in the first half of fiscal 2027 and 0.01x a year earlier, against 0.91x for fiscal 2026, because receivables and contract assets absorb cash as revenue grows. The issuer describes its results as seasonal, so the pattern is not new, but the larger revenue base makes the working capital build larger and leaves cash generation weighted to the second half.
Basis: calculation C43; calculation C42; calculation C41; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 49; 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 53

Supplier finance obligations of USD 367.4 million at 2026-08-01, up from USD 226.4 million at the year end, sit inside accounts payable rather than debt and equal 60.22% of accounts payable. They fund working capital outside the leverage ratios, and if the third-party program ended suppliers could require faster payment, a liquidity call that debt measures do not capture.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 29; calculation C44

The revolver is undrawn with USD 746.4 million of availability. Apart from scheduled amortization the first maturity is USD 500.0 million of 2029 notes in April 2029, followed by USD 1,540.0 million of term loan A in December 2030 and USD 800.0 million of term loan B in January 2033. Funded secured debt is 2.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes, which bring total principal to 3.13x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; calculation C36
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that leverage may already be lower than shown: Building Systems earned a higher Adjusted EBITDA margin than Communications in the first half of fiscal 2027 and contributed to only part of the last twelve months, and total backlog rose between the year end and 2026-08-01. An issuer-stated pro forma EBITDA, or the report for the quarter ended 2026-10-31 that falls after the as-of date, would show whether the improvement holds. A draw on the revolver, a further working capital build or a covenant ratio close to its limit would reverse the view.
### Limitations

The credit agreement and the 2029 notes indenture were not supplied, so covenant definitions, scheduled amortization and baskets are not established and no covenant headroom is stated. Maturities are shown by final maturity because amortization is not itemized, and the cash interest base is built from year-to-date disclosures that only partly reflect the larger borrowings. The Adjusted EBITDA add-back set changed between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, fiscal 2026 had 53 weeks, and the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 is not tabulated as a discrete quarter.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 70, 86

## Findings
### Bottom line

Dycom is a publicly traded, customer-concentrated contractor whose creditors face acquisition-driven releveraging and continuing buybacks rather than sponsor extraction, so governance risk is medium and turns on payout limits that were not supplied.

No sponsor or controlling holder is identified and no dividend has been paid since 1982, but funded debt nearly tripled to buy Power Solutions for USD 2,008.7 million, a new USD 150.0 million buyback was authorized on 2026-08-26, and three customers still supplied 50.2% of fiscal 2026 revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 40, 46; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 30; calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C17
### Key findings

Governance and sponsor risk is medium because the evidence on behavior is good but the legal limits are only summarized. The company has no identified sponsor or controlling holder, has paid no dividend since 1982 and states that it meets its financial covenants, yet it chose debt-funded acquisitions and kept repurchasing shares, and the filings give no basket sizes for payments under the credit agreement or the indenture.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 40, 46, 78; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 21; Source readiness (CP-0)

Customer concentration is the largest business risk but is easing. The three largest customers supplied 50.2% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and three named customers supplied 35.8% of second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue against 52.6% a year earlier, as other customers including Building Systems grew. Because mass markets fiber revenue moved from Lumen to AT&T in fiscal 2027, the comparable measure is the two combined, which fell from 38.4% to 25.4%. Most contracts can be ended for convenience, so one carrier's budget decision can still move revenue sharply.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05

Building Systems is new and acquisition-built, so its contribution to credit strength is not yet proven. It supplied 20.0% of first-half fiscal 2027 revenue after two purchases, against 1.7% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and its Adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.1% is above the 12.9% of Communications, but no pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses is stated and Power Solutions was outside the internal control assessment at the fiscal 2026 year end.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 45; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 122, 128; calculation C16

The acquisitions were paid mainly in cash, funded for Power Solutions by the larger secured credit agreement and a bridge loan, with the sellers taking shares for the rest. Power Solutions cost USD 1,995.9 million at closing, of which 82.41% was cash, and the total was later adjusted to USD 2,008.7 million; National Technology Integrators cost USD 271.4 million, paid with USD 226.4 million of cash and USD 45.0 million of shares. Secured term loans of USD 1,540.0 million and USD 800.0 million now rank ahead of the USD 500.0 million of unsecured 2029 notes, which adds secured claims in front of the notes.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 76, 99; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 19; calculation C06; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C17

Shareholder payments are modest next to acquisition spending but continue. USD 66.1 million of the 2025 repurchase authorization had been used by 2026-08-01, shares were bought at an average USD 359.63 per share in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 against USD 150.93 per share in fiscal 2026, and a new USD 150.0 million program was authorized on 2026-08-26. With the revolver undrawn and covenants stated as met the payments are not straining liquidity today; they would matter if borrowing funded them.

Reporting supports monitoring, with gaps around the new businesses. The auditor reports critical audit matters on revenue recognition and on the valuation of customer relationships acquired with Power Solutions, that business was excluded from the year-end control assessment and National Technology Integrators from the latest quarter's, and the Adjusted EBITDA add-back set changed in fiscal 2027, which weakens comparability.

Backlog supports revenue visibility but is not committed, and results are seasonal. Backlog was USD 12,242 million at 2026-08-01, of which USD 6,472 million falls in the next twelve months, yet customers are not committed to volumes; the weakest quarters end in January and April, and days sales outstanding eased to 101 days from 108 days a year earlier on a pro forma basis.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower risk level is that no sponsor, controlling holder, dividend or related-party fee is described in the filings read, sellers took shares worth USD 351.0 million of the Power Solutions price, the revolver is undrawn with USD 746.4 million of availability, and covenant compliance is stated each quarter. The strongest evidence for a higher level is that Power Solutions was bought mainly with new secured debt, a second acquisition followed within the year, buybacks continued at a much higher share price and were renewed after the larger deal, and three carriers that can end contracts for convenience still supply more than a third of revenue.

The view would move toward low if the credit agreement and indenture show tight payment baskets and the proxy statement confirms no controlling holder or fee arrangements. It would move toward high if the baskets prove wide, if the next quarterly report shows revolver draws funding buybacks or further deals, or if a controlling holder emerges.
### Limitations

- The credit agreement and the indenture were not supplied beyond the issuer's summaries, so the sizes of the dividend, repurchase and acquisition baskets are not established; wide baskets would move the governance level from medium toward high and tight ones toward low.

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so holder percentages, board composition, pay and related-party dealings are not established; a controlling holder or a fee arrangement would change the ownership and leakage conclusions.

- No pro forma EBITDA or integration results for the acquired businesses are stated, although pro forma revenue and net income are, so the judgement that the acquisitions are being absorbed rests on reported segment results and could change when a full year is reported.
- Customer attribution changed in fiscal 2027, so only the combined AT&T and Lumen share is comparable across years; the concentration trend for any single customer is not established.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Power Solutions, LLC, a building infrastructure contractor serving data centers in the Washington D.C., Maryland and Virginia area, was bought on 2025-12-23 after an agreement signed on 2025-11-18. The headline price was USD 1.95 billion; at closing USD 1,644.9 million was paid in cash, shares worth USD 351.0 million were issued to the sellers and USD 64.8 million of seller debt was assumed, for total consideration of USD 1,995.9 million. A working capital adjustment of USD 12.8 million raised the total to USD 2,008.7 million. The deal created the Building Systems segment and is the cause of the rise in funded debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C06; calculation C17

The purchase was financed by amending and restating the credit agreement on 2025-12-23: term loan A rose from USD 440.0 million to USD 1,540.0 million, the revolver from USD 650.0 million to USD 800.0 million, and a USD 600.0 million bridge loan was added, with the revolver and term loan A maturing on 2030-12-23. On 2026-01-27 a USD 800.0 million term loan B maturing on 2033-01-27 refinanced the bridge. The only other debt is the USD 500.0 million of unsecured 2029 notes issued in 2021, so all of the period's new debt is secured bank debt.

National Technology Integrators, a low-voltage engineering and construction firm based in Maryland, was bought on 2026-07-02 for a stated price of USD 275.0 million and total consideration of USD 271.4 million: USD 226.4 million in cash, shares worth USD 45.0 million and USD 12.3 million of seller debt assumed. It joins Building Systems and the revolver stayed undrawn. On 2026-08-26 the board replaced the remaining USD 83.9 million of the repurchase authorization with a new USD 150.0 million program running to February 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 30; calculation C09

spans.text: # CP-2 handoff: Fundamental credit for DYCOM INDUSTRIES INC
## Request

Fundamental credit for DYCOM INDUSTRIES INC (issuer id dy), as of 2026-11-05, for the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesizes the supplied handoffs and filings into one view of business strength, cash conversion, liquidity and the main downside path. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position size.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 (fiscal 2026, 53 weeks) | 2026-03-09 (signature date) | d3cce30e8b33b40ee726fca361a4ac5af2d47cfff9b57a3f36d911b5b73b8e31 | Competition, customers, risk factors, contract terms, cost and labor exposure, interest rate mix |

| 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended August 1, 2026 (second quarter of fiscal 2027) | 2026-08-27 (signature date) | 666dcd463f60ce7cc9d18464ad1e3020b3cf1f9ca79b66ed79bb20b35e9cbf79 | Debt terms and covenants, customer concentration, receivables concentration, backlog, acquisition cash, subsequent event |

| EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl | Second quarter fiscal 2027 results presentation (exhibit to a current report) | 2026-08-26 | db5426dcb5222e08c260f53364ad7255c795bb75eba46ab3566a5906d530e4b2 | Segment margins, backlog, organic growth, liquidity, fiscal 2027 and third-quarter outlook |
Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 a9666727b0d5884c6687d8beafbe462222a8e3c05442392537cb06c514f19ec1.
Supplied handoff: Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 d6a1660a560dc7af94f5244ac4e4c31a6a5d9c7b32f3b0d9a7ad2c49ffe9cffb.
Supplied handoff: Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 667d5cab4376ebc2a840c65db4c7c06319d5ef1ce89103918e18156e062483dc.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Dycom's fundamental credit profile is adequate: liquidity of USD 1,086.5 million, no maturity before April 2029 and backlog of USD 12,242 million support it, but debt-funded acquisitions lifted leverage and a carrier spending deferral is the main downside.

Net debt was 2.73x reported EBITDA at 2026-08-01 against 2.99x at the year end, yet earnings include the acquired businesses only part of the period and cash interest cover of 10.49x is flattered; on run-rate interest it is nearer 6.17x. The Communications margin fell 134 bp in the second quarter while mix lifted the group margin, and free cash flow was USD -54.2 million in the first half.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C19; calculation C33; calculation C13; calculation C23; calculation C36
### Key findings

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main support. Cash plus the undrawn revolver gave USD 1,086.5 million at 2026-08-01, the first maturity is the USD 500.0 million of 2029 notes in April 2029, and the revolver and term loan A fall due in December 2030, so refinancing is not a pressure within two years; only USD 4.0 million of term loan B amortization is itemized for fiscal 2027. Cash did fall 52.05% from the year end after acquisitions, capital expenditures and buybacks, so the cushion is thinner than it was.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19, 21; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C26; calculation C43; calculation C25; calculation C45

Leverage rose with the acquisitions and the improvement so far comes from earnings. Net debt was 2.73x and total debt 3.11x reported EBITDA at 2026-08-01, down from 2.99x and 4.00x at the year end, while carrying-value debt was almost unchanged, and the acquired businesses are in last-twelve-months earnings only from their purchase dates. The fall in leverage is therefore real but partly a timing effect, and a full-period figure is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04

Interest cover on cash paid overstates the burden. Cover of 10.49x uses cash interest that only partly reflects the larger borrowings; first-half interest expense, net, gives 7.64x, and doubling it gives USD 147.0 million of run-rate interest and cover of 6.17x. About 82.39% of principal is variable-rate and the sources show no interest rate hedge, so each 100 bp rise adds USD 23.4 million of interest.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 21; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C21; calculation C22

Margin quality is weaker than the group margin suggests. The group Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 81 bp to 15.7% in the second quarter, but Building Systems at 24.5% is now 19.8% of revenue and the Communications margin fell 134 bp; the issuer says Building Systems also benefited from favorable changes in cost estimates and expects the high-teens to low-twenties for the rest of the year. The margin gain is mix and a possibly one-off lift, not an improvement in the larger business.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 5; calculation C34; calculation C33; calculation C35; calculation C30

Cash conversion is seasonal and thin in the first half. Operating cash flow was 0.14x reported EBITDA and issuer-defined free cash flow USD -54.2 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, against 0.91x and USD 435.3 million (61.84% of EBITDA) for fiscal 2026, as receivables and contract assets absorbed cash while revenue grew. Days sales outstanding eased to 101 days from 108 days, which helps, but the second half has to deliver the year's free cash flow.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C13; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C38

Customer concentration and cancellable backlog are the main business risk. Three named customers supplied 35.8% of second-quarter revenue, four customers hold 44.2% of receivables and contract assets, most agreements can be ended for convenience, and the issuer has already moved about USD 150 million of wireless program revenue into fiscal 2028. Backlog of 1.78x last-twelve-months revenue and organic growth of 16.7% show demand, but a carrier decision to defer work reaches revenue before costs can follow.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 25; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5; calculation C29; calculation C28; calculation C40; calculation C27; calculation C32

Financial policy is the swing factor. The company is buying businesses and shares after nearly tripling its debt since the end of fiscal 2025, a new USD 150.0 million repurchase program was authorized on 2026-08-26, and the issuer ranks organic growth first, then acquisitions, then opportunistic buybacks within its historical range of net leverage. No sponsor or dividend leakage is documented, but the capacity of the debt documents to restrict payments is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C44
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better credit is that demand is running ahead of capacity: backlog rose to USD 12,242 million with organic book-to-bill of 1.4x, organic revenue grew 16.7% in the second quarter, the issuer guides fiscal 2027 revenue to USD 7.48 billion to USD 7.66 billion with a higher group margin, free cash flow was USD 435.3 million in fiscal 2026, and run-rate interest cover is still 6.17x. The strongest evidence for a worse credit is that all of the margin gain is mix, the Communications margin and first-half free cash flow are falling, and net debt rose in the half as cash funded acquisitions and buybacks.

The view would improve if the quarter ended 2026-10-31, which falls after the supplied filings, shows net debt falling with Adjusted EBITDA inside the issuer's outlook of USD 281 million to USD 302 million and the revolver undrawn. It would weaken on any revolver draw to fund buybacks or acquisitions, a Communications margin below 13.6%, further program deferrals beyond USD 150 million, or a Building Systems margin that settles below the high-teens.

Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 5; calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C32; calculation C39; calculation C14; calculation C19; calculation C33; calculation C40; calculation C42
### Limitations

- No peer set, ratings or market data were supplied, so the judgement that the business profile is adequate rests on the issuer's own filings and its standing against other leveraged contractors is not established; a peer comparison could move the profile up or down.

- The issuer does not state how much of the Building Systems margin came from favorable changes in cost estimates, so the normalized margin is not established; a smaller underlying margin would weaken the margin-quality conclusion.

- Run-rate interest is the first half doubled at balances that were close to flat, so it ignores seasonality and any rate move; it supports the view that cash interest cover is flattered but not an exact cover figure.

- The sources split neither maintenance from growth capital expenditure nor working capital by contract type, so how much spending could be cut in a downturn is not established and the downside scenario assumes only that capital expenditure can be slowed.

- The downside is qualitative because covenant definitions and a pro forma earnings base are not available; it shows the order in which pressures arrive, not how far earnings could fall before a covenant is tested.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strength is liquidity with a long runway: USD 1,086.5 million of liquidity, of which USD 746.4 million is undrawn revolver, and no maturity before the USD 500.0 million of 2029 notes mean a spending shock can be absorbed without a refinancing. A second strength is visible demand, with backlog of USD 12,242 million, organic growth of 16.7% and organic book-to-bill of 1.4x, and a third is the Building Systems segment, whose 21.1% six-month margin and 19.8% share of revenue add a higher-margin earnings stream. Customers supplying most materials keeps working capital and input-cost exposure lower than for a self-supplied contractor.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 21; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C36; calculation C32; calculation C37; calculation C47; calculation C30

The main weakness is the leverage step-up on a mostly floating-rate base: debt of 3.11x reported EBITDA, 82.39% variable-rate principal and cash interest cover that is flattered, with run-rate cover of 6.17x. Next is customer concentration, 35.8% of revenue in three names with cancellable agreements. Third is margin quality, where the Communications margin fell 134 bp and the group gain is mix, and fourth is first-half cash conversion of 0.14x. A fifth weakness is discretionary cash use, with acquisitions of USD 238.3 million and buybacks while the capacity of the debt documents to restrict them is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03; calculation C21; calculation C19; calculation C29; calculation C33; calculation C07; calculation C45

### Map: credit-risk transmission
| From | Relationship | Edge type | To | Evidence |
| Carrier spending deferral | Programs pushed to later years | Documentary Fact | Communications revenue | Outlook defers USD 150 million of wireless revenue |
| Communications revenue | Fewer work orders leave labor under-used | Analyst Interpretation | Communications margin | Margin down 134 bp in the second quarter |
| Building Systems mix | Higher-margin segment grows to a fifth | Documentary Fact | Group Adjusted EBITDA margin | Group margin up 81 bp to 15.7% |
| Group Adjusted EBITDA margin | Earnings are the base of every ratio | Documentary Fact | Net debt over EBITDA | Net debt over EBITDA 2.73x at 2026-08-01 |
| Variable-rate debt | Most principal reprices with Term SOFR | Documentary Fact | Cash interest cost | About 82% of debt variable-rate at 2026-01-31 |
| Receivables build | Revenue growth absorbs cash in the first half | Documentary Fact | First-half free cash flow | Free cash flow USD -54.2 million, six months |
| Liquidity | Cash plus undrawn revolver | Documentary Fact | Time before refinancing is needed | Liquidity USD 1,086.5 million; first maturity 2029 |
| Buybacks and acquisitions | Paid from cash on hand | Documentary Fact | Cash balance and net debt | Cash fell 52.05% from the year end |
| Covenant definitions | Not supplied | Insufficient Information | Covenant headroom | Ceiling 4.50x stated; definitions not supplied |
### Company, ownership and revenue drivers

Dycom is a United States specialty contractor that builds and maintains fiber, wireless and utility networks for telecommunications carriers and, since December 2025, electrical and related systems for data centers. Revenue is mostly recurring work under multi-year master service agreements, 86.6% of fiscal 2026 contract revenues, but customers can end most agreements for convenience and are not committed to volumes, so backlog of USD 12,242 million at 2026-08-01, of which USD 6,472 million falls in the next twelve months, signals demand rather than secured revenue. Visibility is good for about a year and exposed to carrier budget decisions beyond that.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 9, 49; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 55; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C31; calculation C36

Ownership adds little structural risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, no dividend has been paid since 1982 and sellers received a minority share of the purchase prices in stock, but the company keeps acquiring businesses and buying back shares, so Business & governance rates governance risk medium and the capacity of the debt documents to restrict payments is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

Revenue growth is demand-led but acquisition-assisted: reported revenue grew 45.57% in the second quarter against organic growth of 16.7%, so acquired businesses supplied most of the increase. Most contracts price each task discretely, do not let the contractor adjust prices for higher fuel costs during a term, and may not reflect rising costs on renewal, so volume rather than price drives revenue, and growth in the larger Communications segment depends on carriers' multi-year programs.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C09; calculation C32
### Cost structure, margins and cash conversion

The group Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 15.7% in the second quarter, 81 bp above a year earlier, only because Building Systems, with a 24.5% margin, is now 19.8% of revenue; the Communications margin fell 134 bp to 13.6%. The issuer expects a slight decline in the Communications margin for the year, citing investment to scale operations and the effect of deferred wireless revenue, and it attributes part of the Building Systems margin to favorable changes in cost estimates, so margins are being defended in the smaller segment, not the larger one.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 5; calculation C34; calculation C33; calculation C35; calculation C30

The cost base is labor-led and partly fixed in a downturn. Customers supply most materials and keep the financial risk of them, which limits working capital and input-price exposure, but each task is priced discretely, the issuer says it may be unable to pass on higher labor and training costs, and tariffs on steel, aluminum, fuel and vehicles are a stated risk. Field labor and fleet are held for backlog, so a volume fall would be expected to lower revenue faster than cost.

Cash conversion is seasonal and was thin in the first half of fiscal 2027. Operating cash flow was 0.14x reported EBITDA and free cash flow USD -54.2 million, against USD 435.3 million, 61.84% of EBITDA, in fiscal 2026, because receivables and contract assets absorbed cash as revenue grew. Capital expenditure was 4.34% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 3.52% in the first half; the sources do not split maintenance from growth spending, so the amount that could be cut is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; calculation C07; calculation C13; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C17
### Competitive forces and external factors

Rivalry and substitution cap pricing power. The industry is fragmented, with large multinational and numerous regional and private competitors, customers can use their own employees, and master agreements have mostly been awarded through competitive bidding. Barriers to entry appear to rest on skilled-labor scale and customer relationships, but the issuer gives no market share, so its standing against competitors is not established.

Buyer power is high and supplier power moderate. Three named customers supplied 35.8% of second-quarter revenue, four customers hold 44.2% of receivables and contract assets, and agreements can be terminated for convenience. Labor is the key input and cannot always be passed through; materials are mostly customer-supplied, though tariffs on steel, aluminum, fuel and vehicles could raise costs.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 25, 26; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 25; calculation C29; calculation C28

External factors matter because they set customer budgets. Demand depends on carriers' and hyperscalers' capital programs, government infrastructure funding, tariff policy and whether artificial-intelligence-driven data-center demand persists; the Building Systems growth case rests on the last of these. Interest rates matter through the variable-rate debt, where each 100 bp rise adds USD 23.4 million of interest.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 18, 24; calculation C22
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: backlog of USD 12,242 million with organic growth of 16.7%; USD 1,086.5 million of liquidity and no maturity before April 2029; a Building Systems margin of 21.1% for the six months; and customer-supplied materials that limit working capital.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 21; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C36; calculation C32; calculation C23; calculation C47

Weaknesses: debt of 3.11x reported EBITDA on a mostly variable-rate base; 35.8% of revenue from three named customers; a Communications margin down 134 bp; and first-half free cash flow of USD -54.2 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C03; calculation C21; calculation C29; calculation C33; calculation C13

Opportunities: contracted long-haul, middle-mile and inside-the-fence fiber builds above USD 1 billion, data-center electrical work in Building Systems, and earnings growth that lowers leverage as the acquired businesses enter a full year.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C46

Threats: carrier program deferrals such as the USD 150 million of wireless revenue moved into fiscal 2028, a reversal in data-center spending, tariff and labor cost increases that cannot be passed on, and rate rises on variable-rate debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 24, 25; EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C40; calculation C22
### Financial profile and credit quality

The business supports debt service better than it supports leverage tolerance. Scale and recurring master agreements give visibility, customer-supplied materials keep working capital contained and capital expenditure was 4.34% of fiscal 2026 revenue, but diversification is limited by customer concentration and the larger Communications business has the weaker margin trend.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-31_dy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 14, 49; calculation C31; calculation C16; calculation C29; calculation C33

Liquidity and refinancing are the strongest dimensions: USD 1,086.5 million of liquidity, USD 746.4 million of undrawn revolver, first maturity in April 2029 and the revolver and term loan A in December 2030. Free cash flow stability is the weakest, with USD 435.3 million in fiscal 2026 but USD -54.2 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, and the financial policy is acquisitive.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 21; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C11; calculation C13

The trend is improving on reported ratios and uncertain on cash. Net leverage fell from 2.99x to 2.73x in six months, but cash fell 52.05% and net debt rose, so deleveraging has come from earnings alone. The missing datapoints are a full-period earnings base for the acquired businesses, covenant definitions and a peer comparison.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C01; calculation C25
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the issuer guides fiscal 2027 revenue to USD 7.48 billion to USD 7.66 billion, now net of about USD 150 million of wireless revenue deferred into fiscal 2028, expects a higher group margin, a slightly lower Communications margin and a Building Systems margin in the high-teens to low-twenties, and guides the third quarter to USD 1.90 billion to USD 1.98 billion of revenue and USD 281 million to USD 302 million of Adjusted EBITDA. These are management's outlook, not evidence, but they imply earnings growth that would lower leverage if net debt stays flat; continued buybacks and acquisitions are the way it would not.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C42

Over three to five years the issuer describes a generational deployment of digital infrastructure projected to continue well into the next decade, which is management language. Tailwinds are carrier fiber programs, long-haul and data-center builds and the order backlog; headwinds are customer concentration, carrier budget timing, tariffs, labor costs and the variable-rate debt. The refinancing order is the USD 500.0 million of notes in April 2029, USD 1,540.0 million of term loan A and the revolver in December 2030 and USD 800.0 million of term loan B in January 2033, so refinancing capacity depends on leverage falling before the 2029 notes and on continued access to secured and unsecured debt markets.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 5; 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C36; calculation C48; calculation C26
### Downside scenario

The most plausible downside starts with a large carrier or hyperscaler customer deferring fiber and wireless programs, as about USD 150 million of wireless revenue has already been deferred. Work orders fall while field labor and fleet are held for backlog, so the Communications margin, already down 134 bp, falls further and the Building Systems margin has to carry the group. EBITDA declines, reported net leverage rises from 2.73x, and first-half free cash flow, already USD -54.2 million, stays negative for longer because receivables are collected from carriers that are also slowing spending.
Basis: EX-99.2_2026-08-26_q22027presentationmateri.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C40; calculation C33; calculation C01; calculation C13

The liquidity effect is bounded by USD 1,086.5 million of liquidity and no maturity before April 2029, and a revenue fall would release receivables and let capital expenditure slow, but about 82.39% variable-rate debt keeps interest running at USD 147.0 million a year and the stated covenant levels are a net leverage ceiling of 4.50x and an interest cover floor of 2.50x on the credit agreement's own definitions. Management levers are capital expenditure, buybacks and acquisitions, and the revolver. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within two years, but covenant headroom is not calculable. Primary downside path: a carrier spending deferral that cuts Communications margin and cash conversion while buybacks or acquisitions are funded from the revolver.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-08-01_dy-20260801.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C23; calculation C21; calculation C18
### Overall credit view

Overall, Dycom presents an adequate business profile supported by backlog, liquidity of USD 1,086.5 million and a Building Systems growth segment, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rose with two debt-funded acquisitions, customer concentration and a weakening Communications margin. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but seasonal, with first-half free cash flow of USD -54.2 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth lowering leverage before the 2029 notes and on financial policy staying within covenants. The primary downside path is a carrier spending deferral against a larger, mostly floating-rate debt load. Further analysis would require a full-period earnings base for the acquired businesses, the covenant definitions and a peer comparison. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: carrier spending deferral.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C23; calculation C13
